ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In the experiment "Exploring Water Absorption and Water Loss in Plant Cells," cells in a stable state in clear water and in a 0.3g/mL sucrose solution are shown in the figure. Compared with Figure 1, is the concentration of cell sap in Figure 2 smaller or greater?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: On the left side of the figure is Figure 1, labeled "clear water"; the contents inside the plant cell are basically close to and fill the range of the cell wall, and no obvious plasmolysis is seen. On the right side is Figure 2, labeled "sucrose solution"; the cell contents have contracted, and a relatively obvious gap appears between them and the cell wall, showing the state after plasmolysis. Then reason: the 0.3 g/mL sucrose solution is an external solution of relatively high concentration, and plant cells will lose water in it; after water loss, the water in the cell sap decreases and the solutes relatively increase, so the concentration of the cell sap rises. Therefore, compared with Figure 1, the concentration of cell sap in Figure 2 is greater.
